meta.method: Pass 1: news-first sweep of wet-season months (Apr–Nov) using Task 26 outlets and qualifying rule. Pass 2 (slimmed 2026-10-18): death queries with no site filter; Oyan Dam / Ogun River / lagoon / water-release / Isheri-Ajegunle-Owode-Agboyi queries; Anadolu once per year; out-of-season Jan–Mar and Dec. Qualifying reports name a Lagos State place and a date, and describe water on streets or in homes. Quotes ≤25 words, verbatim, and taken only from that report's own URL. Dates, numbers and quotes are only those in the source. Areas left as named; not geocoded. Flood date is the flood day, not publication day.
notes: Tuesday 19 Jan 2016: Guardian records Lagos's first rain (~8am, ~1 hour) and 'flash floods in some areas', with no named Lagos street or home. A February blog (thenigerianbloggers) names Oworonshoki homes; not a Task 26 outlet. Lead only; not kept.
March 18 Punch (Meiran Ishaga/Oroja): chronic canal/drainage complaint. Two pupils drowned in 2014, attributed to residents, not a 2016 flood day. Excluded.
April 27 Ojota Bridge / Ikorodu Road rain-flood is The Nation only (Adejare on cane weavers blocking a drain). No Task 26 confirmation. Lead only.

Saturday 14 May: Sunday Vanguard (29 May) visited Iyana Dopemu–Iyana Ipaja 'penultimate Saturday while it was raining'; flood on the road wrecked homes; shop owners relocated. Date worked from publication Sunday. No death reported.

Guardian Sunday magazine 19 Jun describes a recent Lagos street flood (Ahmadu Bello Way, Lawanson, Diya Street Gbagada, Adeshina Street Ijesha). No weekday for the Lagos night; date_confidence period (publication date). The same feature's Sunday 2:30pm–dusk rain and a drowned four-year-old are Ifo LGA, Ogun State, and are not attached as Lagos deaths.

Monday evening 20 Jun into Tuesday 21 Jun: torrential rain. Vanguard (22 Jun) — Lekki roads and homes, Ilubinrin, Park View, Banana Island, Oshodi–Anthony/Oworonsoki. Guardian (22 Jun) — Lekki-Epe Expressway at Awoyaya, Lakowe, Ibeju-Lekki waterlogged. The 'couple swept away a few years back' at UPS/Oworonsoki is historical. No 2016 death.
July: NIHSA/Channels/Punch outlooks only. No Task 26 street/home flood day found.

Saturday night 27 Aug (~8.40–9pm) into Sunday 28 Aug: citywide rain-flood. Punch (29 Aug) names Oworonshoki, Bariga, Ketu/Alapere, Ikorodu/Owutu, Ifako, Lekki; water in homes and churches. LASEMA GM Michael Akindele: millions in property damaged, 'no life was lost'; flood exacerbated by blocked drainages. Vanguard photos: Ladipo Bus Stop on Lagos-Abeokuta Expressway. Punch 'don't panic' (28 Aug) is an Adejare warning, excluded as a standalone report. Unity Estate Ita Oluwo (~50 houses) is Ogun State. Nation/illuminaija/Radio Nigeria are leads confirming the same Sunday; not Task 26 outlets.

Tuesday 6 Sep: Punch and Vanguard — 12-hour / Monday-night rain flooded Ikeja, Iyana-Ipaja, Agege, Ikorodu, Mile 2, Ojo and named mainland streets and homes. Same day, a mudslide collapsed shanties at Kurata/Kuata, Amara Olu Street, Agidingbi; Faisa (Punch 16; Vanguard 18, Faisa Muritala) died, two rescued. LASEMA's Akindele and NEMA's Farinloye call it a mudslide/landslide on a canal-side slum, not a flood drowning. deaths is null; the mudslide is in impacts. Joshua Moses, 27, electrocuted by a fallen pole in River Valley Estate, Ojodu Berger, Ogun State, is not a Lagos flood death. Channels 6 Sep is the collapse only, excluded as a flood report. Lagos–Ibadan Expressway flooding near Mountain Top University is Ogun State; excluded.

Oyan/Ogun riverine episode, mid-September into early October: Guardian 22 Sep — Maidan Orile and Agiliti, Mile 12, Ogun River overflow, homes abandoned. Daily Trust 1 Oct — Agiliti Phase II flood 'penultimate weekend' (17–18 Sep from a Saturday 1 Oct issue); canoes; Oyan Dam alleged by residents, denied by an OORBDA spokesman (gradual releases since May; other tributaries). Punch 6 Oct — 300 houses / 860 households (Farinloye; Soyemi: 15% Oyan release, floodplain building); Lagos areas Agiliti/Maidan, Orile, Owode, Agboyi, Araromi, Ketu, Mile 12, Isheri North GRA, LSDPC Estate. Farinloye: no life lost. Anadolu photo gallery dated 7 Oct: people and cars in flood after Ogun overflow in Lagos. Sikiru Elegushi in Daily Trust: no life lost in that community.

April–May Punch 'Lagos water' at Iludun, Oke-Aro, Ifo LGA is Ogun State. Dried Ogun River at Kara (June) is not a flood. Oct 25 Punch Abule-Oki canal protest recalls deaths 'since 2012', not a dated 2016 day. Otodo Gbame Nov fires are not floods. Premium Times 22 Sep NIHSA national 29 dead does not name a Lagos flood death. TVC, BBC Pidgin, Nairametrics, X:LASEMA/MoE/NEMA: no dated 2016 Lagos street/home flood post reached.

reports.impacts: Sunday Vanguard visited Iyana Dopemu to Iyana Ipaja on the Saturday before last while it rained: one side of the road taken over by flood; shop owners relocated; traffic heavy. The piece says the flood wrecks homes. No death reported.
reports.quote: When Sunday Vanguard visited the site penultimate Saturday while it was raining, shop owners had to relocate
reports.cause_quote: From the Iyana Dopemu junction down to Iyana Ipaja, there is no drainage system

reports.impacts: Recent downpour: Ahmadu Bello Way flooded so salon-car motorists struggled; some cars veered into drainages or uncovered manholes. Lawanson Bus Stop to Pako Bus Stop road flooded; flood into shops. Diya Street Gbagada and Adeshina Street Ijesha flooded. No Lagos death in this article. A four-year-old drowned in Ifo LGA, Ogun State, in a separate section.
reports.quote: Ahmadu Bello Way on Victoria Island was so flooded that motorists found it hard to maneuver
reports.cause_quote: It's unfortunate that people around this area are used to pouring their wastes into the drainage
reports.review_note: 2026-10-18 reviewer: article names no flood day or week (roundup / ongoing inundation); date_confidence set to period; date is the publication date.

reports.impacts: Rain of the past few days, lamented yesterday (Monday 21 Jun): Lekki roads totally submerged; Ilubinrin, Park View and Banana Island said to have been submerged; Oshodi–Anthony–Oworonsoki threatened. Gridlock on Lekki-Epe Expressway. Adewale Akintayo: flood flowing into houses. No death reported. A couple swept away at UPS/Oworonsoki is 'a few years back'.
reports.quote: Our streets have turned into p‘River Nile’ to the extent that flood is flowing into our houses.
reports.cause_quote: the failed portions of the roads also contribute to the flooding that has innundated the area

reports.impacts: Torrential rain from Monday evening continued till yesterday evening (Tuesday 21 Jun): Lekki-Ajah residents in Awoyaya, Lakowe and Ibeju-Lekki exposed to hardship; entire Lekki-Epe Expressway waterlogged; huge traffic gridlock. No death reported.
reports.quote: The entire stretch of the Lekki-Epe Expressway became waterlogged
reports.cause_quote: The situation, according to the residents, becomes aggravated as a result of neglect of some portion of the highway

reports.impacts: Downpours Saturday and Sunday: thousands of Lagos and Ogun residents displaced; streets and homes flooded; some Sunday church services cancelled. Alapere: waist-deep water; TVs and fridges submerged; Bakare and Oriola streets taken over. Bariga streets impassable. LASEMA GM Michael Akindele: distress calls from Oworonshoki, Ifako, Ikorodu and Lekki; property worth millions damaged; no life lost. Unity Estate Ita Oluwo (~50 houses, ~200 displaced) is Ogun State.
reports.quote: downpours on Saturday and Sunday left many streets and homes flooded
reports.cause_quote: The flood was exacerbated by blockages of some of the major drainages in the affected areas

reports.impacts: Photo captions: flood at Ladipo Bus Stop along Lagos-Abeokuta Express Road before Oshodi after heavy downpour that started about 9pm Saturday and lasted till Sunday evening. No death reported.
reports.quote: Flood at Ladipo Bus Stop along Lagos Abeokuta express road before Oshodi due to heavy down pour
reports.cause_quote: heavy down pour which started at about 9pm on Saturday and lasted till Sunday evening

reports.impacts: Rain for about 12 hours: residents abandoned houses; streets in Egbeda and Idimu flooded; named streets' houses flooded; cars and buses submerged on a Dopemu street. Same Tuesday: mudslide at Kurata slum, Dosumu Street off Amara Olu Road, Agidingbi, killed 16-year-old Faisa (newly wed); two others rescued. LASEMA GM Akindele: three trapped in mud, one recovered dead. NEMA SW Ibrahim Farinloye: 'a mudslide which collapsed on shanties'. Joshua Moses, 27, electrocuted by a fallen pole at River Valley Estate, Ojodu Berger, Ogun State. The mudslide and Ogun electrocution are not flood drownings.
reports.quote: The rainfall, which lasted for about 12 hours in several areas in Lagos and Ogun states, forced some residents to abandon their houses
reports.cause_quote: The rainfall, which lasted for about 12 hours in several areas in Lagos and Ogun states, forced some residents to abandon their houses

areas: Kuata, Amara-Olu Street, Mechanic Village, Agidingbi, Ikeja
reports.impacts: Persistent rainfall from late Monday evening: heavy flooding and traffic gridlock in Ikeja, Iyana-Ipaja, Agege, Ikorodu, Mile 2, Ojo and others. Same Tuesday morning: mudslide at Kuata/Amara-Olu Street, Agidingbi; Faisa Muritala recovered dead (article gives age 18); two rescued. LASEMA GM Micheal Akindele: distress call 10.54am 6 Sep 2016; three trapped under mud; one adult female lost her life. Not reported as a flood drowning.
reports.quote: The persistent rainfall, which started late Monday evening, resulted in heavy flooding across the metropolis.
reports.cause_quote: The persistent rainfall, which started late Monday evening, resulted in heavy flooding across the metropolis.

reports.impacts: Incessant downpour caused Ogun River to overflow: flood took over Maidan Orile and Agiliti; many homeless or abandoned the area; property worth millions of naira lost; community-built link bridge to Mile 12 threatened. No death reported.
reports.quote: They are groaning under the heavy flood that has taken over their community due to the incessant downpour
reports.cause_quote: incessant downpour in the state which has caused Ogun River to overflow its banks
reports.review_note: 2026-10-18 reviewer: article names no flood day or week (roundup / ongoing inundation); date_confidence set to period; date is the publication date.

reports.impacts: Flood that visited Agiliti Phase II 'penultimate weekend' (from Saturday 1 Oct issue: 17–18 Sep): homes relocated from; vehicular movement paralysed; residents using canoes; businesses collapsed from Agiliti Phase 1 to Itowolo and Ajegunle; pupils kept from school. Mummy Mariam: water here for the past two weeks. Sikiru Elegushi: no life has been lost since the community started experiencing the flood. OORBDA spokesman: not true that dam releases flood Lagos; gradual opening since May; other tributaries and recent rain.
reports.quote: vehicular movement has been paralyzed in the rural area while residents now resort to using canoes
reports.cause_quote: We are used to it, whenever the dam is open and water is released, the whole community is flooded
reports.cause_who: Taiwo Mohammed, Oluwabukumi Street, Agiliti Phase II

reports.impacts: No fewer than 300 houses flooded and 860 households displaced after Oyan Dam water opened (Farinloye; same figures in the lead). Residents: floodwater about two weeks ago, volume increased last week, houses overrun; some reach homes by canoe (N100–N500). Riverview Estate chairman Abayomi Akinde: flooding started about three weeks ago; no OORBDA notice. OORBDA MD Akintunde Soyemi: 15% controlled release; floodplain building. Farinloye: no life was lost. Kara and Warewa in Ifo LGA, Ogun State, also named in his assessment.
reports.quote: No fewer than 300 houses have been flooded and 860 households displaced following the opening of Oyan Dam water
reports.cause_quote: Most of those flooded places are in the flood plain of Ogun River
reports.cause_who: Akintunde Soyemi, Managing Director, Ogun/Osun River Basin Development Authority

reports.impacts: Photo gallery dated 7 Oct 2016: people walking in a flooded area, a car in flood water, people on boats, after a day-long torrential rain caused the Ogun river to overflow in Lagos. No death stated.
reports.quote: People walk in a flooded area after the Ogun region flooded following a day long torrential rain
reports.cause_quote: a day long torrential rain caused Ogun river to overflow in Lagos, Nigeria on October 7, 2016
